TIP-OFF

Basketball School

TIP-OFF

is our opening huddle where coaches welcome the players as a group and set the expectations for the day. The Tip-Off should take no longer than 5 minutes to maximize player attention spans. There are 5 parts that should be covered in every Tip-Off:

CALL IN

Players are verbally called in to huddle up and stand in a circle with all players and coaches if numbers allow (for larger groups, coaches may need to stand in front of the players).

CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

COMMENCEMENT

Players are primed and prepped for the start of the camp.

CHEER

Players and coaches give an enthusiastic and excited cheer together!

WARM UP

Basketball School

TEAM DRIBBLE KNOCKOUT WITH LOADS

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no baskets needed)

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per player

### DESCRIPTION

Players will play standard dribble knockout. They will play in a confined space (e.g. the half-court or only inside the 3PT area), attempting to knock another player ball outside the space while dribbling their own ball. If a player gets knocked out, they have to go and score a jump shot outside the paint on a free basket before they are allowed to rejoin the game.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Players can only dribble with their weak hand.
- Players must skip or move backwards continuously while playing knockout.
- Players are divided into two equal teams, with one team wearing bibs. Once a player is out, they become a supporter and must cheer for their team. The team to get all opposing players out first is the winner.

### SCORING

Players get 1 point for every player they knock out.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Developing ball manipulation skills

### STAFF ROLE

- Officiate double dribbles and out of bounds violations.
- Encourage players to keep their eyes up and scan the floor.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- Where is the space?
- How could you work with a teammate to get another player out?

MODULE 7: FULL OUTLINE

WARM UP

Basketball School

RANDOM MOVEMENT SHOOTING

10 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per player

### DESCRIPTION

Players will explore using various functional movements, incorporating this into their shooting. To begin with, players will find a different way to lunge or squat every time. After completing two lunges or squats, they will shoot the ball from any location outside the paint. After this, they must move to a new location and lunge or squat differently before the shot.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Hop in a different way three times before shooting.
- Complete any type of movement on the floor before exploding up and shooting.
- Create your own movement! This could include anything creative before the shot.

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players change locations.
- Encourage players to try new and creative movements.

### SCORING

N/A

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Adaptive shooting

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- Can you find a more creative way to move?!

GAME TIME

Basketball School

GAME TIME

is where players participate in different activities and games designed to stimulate their growth and development.

These activities have been carefully created to mimic the game of basketball. With the NBA Basketball School Camp Curriculum, players develop technically and tactically through the actual act of playing basketball itself.

Each Game Time activity is clearly described and presented in the following format: name, time, space, equipment, description, scoring, types of loads, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions. Coaches are encouraged to utilize the information presented and to expand on those ideas in a way that would be most meaningful to their players.

MODULE 7: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

2-ON-1 BALL ON HIP

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

Players in groups of three with a maximum of four groups per basket. The defender will start on the hip of an offensive player, with the other offensive player spaced anywhere single gap spacing away (e.g. wing in relation to top, corner in relation to wing, etc). As soon as the offensive player removes the ball from the hip of the defender, the 2-on-1 is live. The offense has a maximum of two passes to find an open shot. They can pass and drive but are not allowed to enter the paint.

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Players can score lay-ups after the first pass.
- Players cannot cut or receive the ball in the lava. This means they must get out to space quickly.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players understand the single gap.
- Emphasize decisions to shoot, drive, or pass based on who is in more space.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- Where is the single gap?
- Where is your space to exit to after the first pass?

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Getting out to space after passing when an advantage exists
- Working on passing out of a drive and kick with a defender on the hip

MODULE 7: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

2-ON-2 FIXED SPOT

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per basket

#### DESCRIPTION

Each basket needs one ball and several groups of two players. One group will begin on offense with a second group of defenders matching up. Players must play from the same spacing on offense every time: the ball on a wing and the other offensive player spaced in the weakside dunker spot. Other groups will wait their turn at the baseline. The on-ball defender will start blind to the offense, with their heels on the 3PT line facing the basket. The offense will hold the ball and place it on the defender back. The off-ball defender can start in a gap or help position depending on their match up placement on the 3PT line. As soon as they lift the ball from the defense back, it becomes a live 2-on-2. Games go until a basket is scored, there is a defensive stop, or the ball goes out of bounds.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets. Defensive players will get 2 points for defensive stops (defensive rebound or forced turnover).

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating space and keeping advantage
- Finding space from the dunker (attempting to score inside the smile)
- Attacking the help defense
- Scoring off 2-on-1 advantages
- Helping and recovering on defense

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- For younger players, the lava is the paint area. Offensive players cannot catch the ball inside the paint unless they are cutting to the basket. A turnover occurs if players receive the ball in the lava (within the paint).
- Inside the 3PT line is lava. If players do not score off the first drive, then players must re-space either to weakside dunker or beyond the 3PT line.
- The offense can only score a rim finish or 3PT shot.
- For younger players, the mid-range is still permitted.
- Remove 1 defender and play 2-on-1.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Help players with the start spacing, ensuring they utilize the wing and weakside dunker.
- Officiate the lava load.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- What other positions could you explore playing from?
- What can the defense do to ensure the offense does not score off the first drive?

MODULE 7: FULL OUTLINE

GAME TIME

Basketball School

2-ON-1 CONVERSION INTO 1-ON-2 BACK

16 MIN

BINDING YES NO

#### PLAYING SPACE

All available baskets (cut the court along rim line to create two playing spaces per basket)

#### EQUIPMENT

1 ball per group

#### DESCRIPTION

The offense and defense must stay in half of the full-court area, playing from sideline to rim line. Two offensive players will start in any position along the half-court line. This should be different every time. One defender will begin in-between both players. As soon as the defender moves off the line, the offense can move and a live 2-on-1 begins. The offense must find a way to score a rim finish within six seconds. The moment the defender gets the ball (either after a score or a stop), they then have eight seconds to score a touchdown by dribbling to the half-court line. The offense transitions to defense and attempts to gain a stop by trapping.

#### SCORING

Offensive players will get 2 points or 3 points for made baskets in the 2-on-1. The defender will get 3 points for a successful touchdown in the 1-on-2.

#### KEY CONCEPTS

- Creating space and keeping advantage
- Transition offense and defense

#### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- The offense only has two passes to score a rim finish on the first possession.
- The offense begins off a sideline or baseline inbound, instead of advancing the ball from half-court.
- If the defense steals the ball in the 1-on-2, they must attempt to convert this into a made basket within 4 seconds.

#### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure players stay in their respective areas.
- Reinforce score, drive, or pass decisions in 2-on-1 advantage.

#### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- Did the defender commit to stopping you?
- How could you convert the 2-on-1 faster?
